newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's EPR rebels declare ceasefire in Guerrero.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's EPR rebels declare ceasefire in Guerrero.

text.p: Mexico's Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) guerrillas on Wednesday declared a month-long ceasefire in the southern state of Guerrero, saying it aimed to avoid disrupting local elections due on Oct. 6.
In a statement made available to Reuters by TV Azteca, the EPR said its high command called the ceasefire from midnight Wednesday (0500 GMT on Thursday) to 8:30 p.m. Oct. 27 (0130 GMT on Oct. 28).
"During this period, EPR units in our state of Guerrero will not carry out any offensive military action against police and military forces of the anti-popular government," the statement said.
It said it would only open fire if its forces considered themselves "in imminent danger" of attack.
The EPR first appeared in Guerrero state on June 28, and two months later hit police and military targets in several states in a wave of attacks that led to at least 20 deaths.
Since then head-on attacks have died down. It was the first time the rebels have declared any form of ceasefire.

In its statement, the EPR acknowledged that one of its fighters, Benjamin Avila Blanco, was shot dead by soldiers on Sept. 16 in Guerrero during a clash with soldiers. It claimed that five soldiers were also killed, but the army said only two of its troops were wounded.
The rebels insisted they supported the vote for town mayors and state Congress in Guerrero, though the run-up has been marred by incidents of violence.
"The EPR in no way is opposed the the electoral struggle of the people nor does it seek to block it," the rebels said.

It charged that the electoral process was already tilted in favour of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has ruled Mexico and the vast majority of its state and local government offices for 67 years.
Declaring that the opposition was at a disadvantage, it urged Mexicans to stand up for their voting rights.
"We call on the people to stop the government imposing itself above and beyond the popular will, and to defend to the ultimate consequences the respect for the vote," it said.

The major leftist force in the state, the Democratic Revolution Party, says some of its candidates, including a national senator, have already been roughed up by government security forces while campaigning in Guerrero.

Troops have poured into the dirt-poor state, home of the plush Pacific tourist resort of Acapulco, since the EPR first rose up against the government of President Ernesto Zedillo. But so far they have failed to make a significant dent in the shadowy rebel movement.
